title: Shortest Word Distance III
summary: Given an array of strings wordsDict and two strings word1 and word2 that are part of the array, find the minimum distance between their occurrences.
statement: Given an array of strings wordsDict and two strings word1 and word2 that are part of the array, find the minimum distance between their occurrences. word1 and word2 are distinct words in the array, though they can be identical.
constraints: words contains 1–100000 lowercase words of length 1–10. Both targets occur; if they are equal, that word occurs at least twice.
Return the minimum index distance between two INDIVIDUAL occurrences. When word1==word2, an occurrence cannot be paired with itself.
hints: First decide whether the two target strings are equal.
For distinct targets, track both latest positions. For one repeated target, track its previous occurrence only.
On each matching repeated word, measure index-previous before replacing previous. Otherwise use the two-target scan.
The guarantee refers to two individual occurrences, so a same-word answer is always positive.
editorial: The distinct-target branch is the ordinary two-latest-index scan. In the equal-target branch, the minimum gap must occur between consecutive occurrences in occurrence order; skipping an intervening occurrence only increases the distance. The independent oracle explicitly lists positions and either checks consecutive gaps or every cross-target pair.
